purpose: Can an independently mapped East Antarctic site-scale never-used habitat risk set support a NEW colonization mechanism after ruling out prior art, without falsely joining Cape Crozier 2021 nest patches?

originals.unit: individual ice-free island or coastal rocky outcrop, coastal site polygon/reference
site x split-year breeding season, source observational presence/absence
site x species x breeding season SEARCH EVENT, explicit presence/absence/nonreporting and absence confidence

cross_domain_exclusions: Cape Crozier ~169.2 E is OUTSIDE the published source longitudinal footprint, so East Antarctic never-used site rows do NOT provide comparable unused patches around the Cox 2021/22 50 nests
2016/2025 source unit is geographically distinct rocky island/outcrop, not an individual 3-10m nest/guano patch. No nesting-fate or founder identity join
potentially suitable land is not a demonstration of weather/snow, marine access or site-specific breeding feasibility in a given season
zero current presence reports and no documented search MUST NOT be conflated with true site absence
2025 publication already investigated surveyed/unsurveyed site classes and 2017 already rejected 16/16 apparent satellite turnover events

prior_art.Southwell et al 2017: doi:10.1642/AUK-16-125.1; all 16 evaluated apparent East Antarctic colonization/extinction events false
prior_art.Southwell et al 2025: doi:10.1111/ddi.70066; 248 occupied Adelie sites and 1633 conservative /3762 optimistic absent sites, 36.1% vs77.0% search effort
prior_art.Cox et al 2024: doi:10.1007/s00300-024-03246-9; 50 Cape Crozier exact nest locations, not source-compatible with AADC East Antarctic control sites

source_trial.method: HEAD and bounded GET, official origin only, up to 3 known URLs; inspect verified archive magic/member names or response headers, no biological event rows opened
